note: MVP vertical slice: one adaptive journey for consonant doubling (EN.FND.SPL.inflections#double_short). Everything here is provisional and awaits educator review: the 8 assessment questions (drafts spl.infl.18-25), the three strategy lessons and the hint wording. The questions are hand-written candidates like the rest of the bank; the guided-practice words are generated items and stay practice-only. Content-validation gate: every journey question added here carries evidence_status "provisional", so answers to it are recorded and shown at rule level as provisional, but never change the capability estimate. The last hint level of each strategy is a worked example that shows the answer; it is recorded as revealing the answer.

items.prompt: Write the -ing form of swim: She is ___ in the lake.
items.rationale: Doubles the final consonant of a short one-syllable verb (swim → swimming). Journey copy of spl.infl.02: provisional until educator-approved. The bank item spl.infl.02 is unchanged.

items.prompt: Write the -ing form of run: Look, the dog is ___ after the ball.
items.rationale: Doubles the final consonant of a short one-syllable verb (run → running). Journey copy of spl.infl.11: provisional until educator-approved. The bank item spl.infl.11 is unchanged.

items.prompt: Write the -ing form of chop: Dad is ___ the onions.
items.rationale: One short vowel, one final consonant: double before -ing.

items.rationale: Two vowel letters (ou) before the last consonant: nothing doubles. Contrast for the reassessment after teaching: provisional until educator-approved.

items.rationale: Two vowel letters (ea) before the last consonant: nothing doubles. Contrast for the reassessment after teaching: provisional until educator-approved.

independent.note: Assessment, reassessment and retention questions are taken in this order, unseen ones only. The delayed check uses only items where the rule applies; the reassessment after teaching asks an apply item, a contrast, then an apply item. Every journey question is provisional (evidence_status). swim and run are journey copies (spl.infl.j02, j11) of bank items spl.infl.02 and 11, so the bank items keep their status; a word the learner has already answered elsewhere counts as seen. Contrasts 26-31 were added so that every reassessment includes an unfamiliar item where the rule must not be applied; they are provisional like the rest.

strategies.name: Rule and worked examples

lesson.title: Doubling the last letter
steps: Look at the end of the word.
One vowel, then one consonant? Double the consonant before -ing, -ed, -er or -est.
Two consonants at the end, or two vowels before the last letter? Just add the ending.
lesson.tip: hopping comes from hop; hoping comes from hope.

hints: Look at the end of the word: one vowel, then one consonant?
{base} ends in one vowel and one consonant ({last}). What happens to the {last}?
Worked example (this shows the answer): {base} ends in one vowel and one consonant, so the {last} doubles: {base} + {last} + {ending} = {word}.

strategies.name: Listen for the short vowel

lesson.title: Listen to the vowel
steps: Do you hear a short vowel, as in cat, sit, hop or cup?
A short vowel before one consonant needs a double letter to stay short: tap → tapping.

examples.note: short a doubles; long a does not

lesson.tip: The double letter is a guard that keeps the vowel short.

hints: Say {base} out loud. Is the vowel short, as in cat or sit?
The short vowel needs a guard: the {last} doubles.
Worked example (this shows the answer): say {base}, then double the {last} and add the ending: {base} + {last} + {ending} = {word}.

strategies.name: Build the word in parts

lesson.title: Build the word in three parts
steps: Part 2: an extra copy of the last letter, only if the root ends in one vowel + one consonant (p).
Part 3: the ending (-ing). Put them together: hop + p + ing = hopping.

examples.note: o then p: add a p

lesson.tip: Sort first: does it need the extra letter or not?

hints: Split it: {base} | ? | {ending}. Does {base} end in one vowel and one consonant?
Yes, so the middle part is another {last}.
